newsitem.title: HUNGARY: CZECH CROWN BATTLE HELPS SUPPORT FORINT- DEALER.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CROWN BATTLE HELPS SUPPORT FORINT- DEALER.

text.p: Hungary's forint eased against the dollar Tuesday afternoon, but remained steady versus the central bank's resistance level (NBH bid), dealers said.
The forint ended at 181.02/07 to the dollar, down from 180.90 at midday as it tracked the dollar/mark, dealers said.
A dealer said foreign investors' activity was strong and probably part of the investors, who had pulled out of the Czech market, bought forints, planning bond or equity purchases.
Short-sellings pushed the Czech crown to record lows last week, prompting the Czech central bank to intervene.
"I think that those who left the Czechs, have extra money and place it here," said ING Bank's Attila Behan.
Other dealers said they did not feel that the forint buying interest of foreign investors had increased.

"The market was as usual," Unicbank's Gabor Liener said, adding that the forint was strong related to the central bank bid as many market players expected the monthly 1.1 percent forint devaluation to be cut in the second half of 1997.

Dealers and analysts agreed that the forint was unlikely to face an attack similar to the Czech crown as Hungary's balance of payment position was stable and forint investments seemed to offer satisfactory yields to foreign investors.
"The forint will stay at the (central bank) bid tomorrow and later," Attila Behan said.
(National Bank of Hungary (NBH) basket: 30 pct dollar + 70 pct mark. The NBH's intervention range is 4.5 percent wide.)
